B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No MCP-specific fee is stated in the reviewed official material. MCP is beta and access is limited to some customers; the official pricing page provides no public plan amounts.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Personio sells Core and Core Pro plans with individually quoted pricing. The official page says pricing depends on company size and selected features or apps.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The official page describes pricing according to employee count and selected features/apps; it does not state amounts. It also describes an annual subscription minimum of 12 months and a one-time setup fee whose amount depends on company size.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Beta availability is limited. A Personio administrator enables general AI access and MCP for the organization; write access is a separate opt-in. Employee access follows their Personio permissions. AI-tool accounts and permissions are also needed; some clients may require paid subscriptions or client-side administrator permissions. Heavy or scripted usage is rate-limited.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Personio controls beta availability and server-side organization/tool/attribute settings; organization administrators enable MCP and configure controls; authenticated users’ Personio roles limit data access; AI-tool administrators/users configure client access and approvals.

The official article says changes to the MCP setting are recorded for auditability, but does not say that tool calls or returned data are logged by the MCP server.

The input endpoint returned HTTP 401 and a WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata URL. Both protected-resource documents advertise bearer tokens in the header and identify https://mcp.app.personio.com/mcp as the resource. The authorization-server metadata lists authorization_code and refresh_token grants; S256 PKCE; token endpoint auth methods none, client_secret_basic, and client_secret_post; and scopes openid, profile, email, offline_access, and mcp:access. It advertises no registration_endpoint. Revocation is advertised at https://login.personio.com/oauth/revoke. Token lifetime is not stated. The official setup article says users retrieve an OAuth client ID from Personio settings and leave the client secret empty.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official docs describe reads and limited writes, but the available Composio actions are all read-oriented. No tool annotations are published. 2. Personio says write access is a separate opt-in and recommends AI-client approval for write actions and sensitive reads; server-enforced per-call confirmation is not documented. Approval of time off is listed as coming soon. 3. OAuth scopes are listed above. The docs say access mirrors the authenticated user's Personio permissions; an administrator enables MCP and controls tools and attributes. Client setup uses an OAuth client ID; redirect-URI approval and token lifetime are not documented. 4. No read-only endpoint or URL toolset filters are documented. Writes have a separate organization toggle; beta availability is limited. 5. Administrators can hide selected employee attributes, including address or IBAN. Docs state Personio rejects disabled tools and restricted attributes regardless of AI-client settings. Document contents are not returned by the Composio-listed document action. 6. Large queries are paginated; heavy or scripted usage is rate-limited. No numeric quota, bulk cap, time cap, or call cost is stated. 7. Validation, unknown-argument handling, coercion, and operator overrides are unknown. 8. Changes to MCP settings are recorded for auditability. MCP-call logging and telemetry are unknown. 9. Official docs invite users to give beta feedback in Personio settings. No feedback tool is in the catalogue's 10-action list. No tool-result upsell evidence found. 10. Official setup guidance recommends approval controls and checking results; these are client/user instructions, not documented server enforcement. No server-delivered skills were found. 11. Memory/state effects are unknown. 12. The input endpoint and documented app.personio.com endpoint have different hostnames; the protected-resource metadata advertises a third resource URI. Their relationship is not clarified. 13. No raw API, SQL, script, or arbitrary execution tool appears in the 10-action third-party list; input endpoint's complete list is unavailable.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The official docs recommend user/client checks: “Always confirm important outputs before you act on data or approve changes, including Write actions like time off requests.” They recommend setting AI-tool approval for write actions and sensitive reads. The docs also advise using attribute-level scoping instead of disabling core tools. These are documented recommendations; only the organization-level tool and attribute boundaries are described as enforced by Personio.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Personio says access mirrors the authenticated user's permissions and the server does not grant additional access. It says disabled tools and restricted attributes are refused by Personio regardless of AI-tool settings, and MCP setting changes are recorded for auditability. It warns that after an AI tool accesses data, Personio can no longer trace that tool's subsequent use; that use is subject to the AI vendor's privacy and processing agreement.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The server is disabled by default; write access is a separate opt-in. Administrators can disable individual tools and hide selected person attributes. Personio says the server is in beta and not available to everyone.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The official article documents server-side organization controls and role-based access, but no public implementation code was found to verify their internal enforcement. The article explicitly describes disabled tools and restricted attributes as refused server-side. Approval recommendations are assigned to AI-tool settings/users, not established as MCP-server enforcement. Audit logging is stated for setting changes; tool-call logging is not established.

contradictions: The input is https://mcp.personio.de/mcp, while Personio's beta setup article instructs users to connect to https://app.personio.com/mcp. The input endpoint's protected-resource metadata identifies https://mcp.app.personio.com/mcp as the resource. The source material does not explain whether these hosts are aliases or separate deployments.

Personio's official article describes limited write operations such as requesting time off, but the Composio catalogue's 10 listed actions are read-oriented and contain no write action. The catalogue may expose a different integration surface.

The official article says time-off approval is coming soon; the same page's capability table describes an approval use case. Its status is therefore described as forthcoming rather than currently available.
observations_for_research: The official beta documentation describes two layers of control: Personio administrator settings establish organization-wide boundaries, while AI-client settings can narrow access per tool and user.
The OAuth protected-resource scopes include mcp:access and identity/offline-access scopes, while role-level and attribute-level permissions are described separately in product documentation.

Personio's official beta article documents capability categories and configuration behavior but does not publish exact tool names or schemas. Third-party catalogue coverage therefore cannot establish the input endpoint's complete action set.
